Set \(u=w^{3}\). The equation becomes the cubic
\[
1121610\sqrt{3270}\,u^{3}-407425607\,u^{2}+10360232=0,
\]
which has three real roots \(u_{1}<0<u_{2}<u_{3}\); hence \(k=3\) and
\(w_{1}=u_{1}^{1/3}<w_{2}=u_{2}^{1/3}<w_{3}=u_{3}^{1/3}\).
Exact evaluation gives
\[
w_{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3270}}{105},\qquad
w_{1,3}=\mp\sqrt{\frac{811}{436}\mp\frac{5\sqrt{18705}}{436}},
\]
so that
\[
m=(w_{1}+w_{3})w_{2}=\frac57.
\]

Therefore \(\displaystyle \frac{63m}{5}=9\), and the expression to minimize is
\[
E=\frac{x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3}}{xyz}+\frac{9\sqrt[3]{xyz}}{x+y+z},
\]
which is homogeneous of degree \(0\).  Impose \(xyz=1\); then
\[
E=x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3}+\frac{9}{x+y+z}.
\]
By the power-mean inequality,
\(x^{3}+y^{3}+z^{3}\ge\frac{(x+y+z)^{3}}{9}\).
Let \(p=x+y+z\); AM–GM gives \(p\ge3\), and
\[
E\ge \frac{p^{3}}{9}+\frac{9}{p}\equiv f(p).
\]
Since \(f'(p)=\frac{p^{2}}{3}-\frac{9}{p^{2}}>0\) for \(p\ge3\),
\(f(p)\ge f(3)=3+3=6\).
Equality holds at \(x=y=z=1\), so the minimum value is \(6\).
